_note: Briefs for the portraits of the Mímir cards (images/portraits/BRIEF.md explains them). Read by edda-site/tools/gen_portraits.py. subjects: kind (person, animal, place, thing), subject (what must be seen), ref (a cut-out in ref/<id>.jpg is the character reference), length (three-quarter or whole, where half-length would lose the attribute), pair / pair_of + differs (the two are drawn in one sheet, facing each other). lights + relight: the prompt that turns a chosen picture into its dusk and night versions (gen_portraits.py --relight).
reference: Use the attached picture only as the character reference: the same person, face, hair, clothing colours and objects. Redraw the figure alone. Do not copy the neighbours or the background.
rules: Plain quiet background, the same in every panel. No text, no letters, no runes, no labels, no border, no frame, no signature, no other people. No horned or winged helmets; clothing and gear of the Viking Age.

format.person: A single figure, {length}, head centred in the width, the top of the head one eighth down from the top edge, the eyes one third down, the attribute in front and fully visible inside the central square.
format.animal: The whole animal alone, filling most of the frame, its most telling outline clear.
format.place: The whole of it alone, one clear shape filling most of the frame.
format.thing: The object alone, lying or hanging, no hand, filling most of the frame.

person: three-quarter view facing slightly left, calm, the attribute held in front
in the middle of the act the figure is known for, the attribute in use
seated or at rest, a little further back so that more of the figure shows
animal: three-quarter view, the head towards the viewer
place: closer, on the most telling part
whole, from a little further away
thing: closer, on the most telling detail

A.name: The plates' own style
A.text: Painted illustration with fine ink outline, muted earth colours (ochre, rust red, slate blue, moss green) on warm parchment, soft flat light, small touches of gold; the same hand as the attached reference. Background: bare warm parchment with a faint wash behind the figure.

B.name: Woodcut / linocut
B.text: Hand-printed linocut: bold black outline and carved hatching, three flat colours only (black, one rust red, one muted blue-green) on cream paper, slight unevenness of ink as in a real print. Strong simple shapes, almost no background: a few carved lines for ground or sky.

C.name: Icelandic paper manuscript
C.text: In the manner of the illustrated Icelandic Edda manuscripts of the 17th and 18th centuries: naive pen drawing in brown-black ink with flat watercolour washes (red, yellow ochre, blue, green), stiff charm, simple faces, plain laid paper with slight foxing. No lettering anywhere.

D.name: Viking Age ornament
D.text: Flat stylised figure in the manner of Viking Age picture stones and metalwork: clear silhouette, interlace and ribbon ornament inside the shapes, limited palette of stone grey, iron black, red ochre and a little gold, on a rough pale stone ground. Still readable as a person or animal at a glance.

E.name: Book illustration, about 1900
E.text: Ink-and-watercolour book illustration in the Nordic manner of about 1900: confident pen line, large calm areas of muted colour, a low horizon or a single tree or wave as setting, an art-nouveau sense of design without ornament borders. Dignified, a little melancholy.

B2.name: Linocut, winter
B2.text: Hand-printed linocut: bold outline and carved hatching, slight unevenness of ink as in a real print. Strong simple shapes, almost no background: a few carved lines for ground or sky. Three flat colours only: black, slate blue and a pale grey-blue, on cool white paper. A cold, quiet northern light.

B3.name: Linocut, ochre and moss
B3.text: Hand-printed linocut: bold outline and carved hatching, slight unevenness of ink as in a real print. Strong simple shapes, almost no background: a few carved lines for ground or sky. Three flat colours only: black, yellow ochre and moss green, on cream paper. Warm, earthy, like late summer.

B4.name: Linocut, indigo and gold
B4.text: Hand-printed linocut: bold outline and carved hatching, slight unevenness of ink as in a real print. Strong simple shapes, almost no background: a few carved lines for ground or sky. The key block in deep indigo instead of black; two more flat colours only: gold ochre and a soft brick red, on warm off-white paper.

B5.name: Linocut, hand-coloured
B5.text: Hand-printed linocut: bold outline and carved hatching, slight unevenness of ink as in a real print. Strong simple shapes, almost no background: a few carved lines for ground or sky. The print in black only, then hand-tinted with thin, uneven watercolour washes in muted natural colours (any colours the subject needs), the paper showing through.

odin.subject: Óðinn: an old man with one eye. The other eye is gone, given for a drink from Mímir's well: an empty, sunken eye socket, closed, with an old scar across the lid, shown openly. No eye patch, no band, no cover over it, and not hidden by the hat brim (the reference wrongly shows a patch; do not copy it). Grey beard, dark blue cloak and wide hat; the spear Gungnir upright in his hand; a gold arm-ring. No ravens and no wolves in the picture.
